clue.text: Choose to have Ronald in charge with this type of brain

parts.note: to choose by vote is to elect
Ron is the short form of the name Ronald

explanation.surface: Someone recommends putting Ronald in charge because of his kind of mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer is often called an electronic brain, the adjective naming that kind of machine mind.

clue.text: A heavy role

definitions.meaning: a heavy metal, the dense grey element used for weights and pipes
the principal part in a play or film

explanation.surface: Casting talk: a weighty part for an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal is proverbially heavy, and the starring part in a show is the main acting role.

clue.text: Senior officer with trim slice of meat

parts.note: COL is the abbreviation for colonel, a senior army officer
to lop is to trim by cutting off branches

explanation.surface: A colonel trims a cut of meat at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: COLLOP is an old British and Scottish word for a thin slice of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A collop is a dialect term for an escalope or thin cut of meat.

clue.text: Others with skill begin again

parts.note: the rest means the others, those remaining
art can mean skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: The remaining people use their skill to start over.
explanation.definitionFit: To restart is to start once more after stopping.

clue.text: No litter for this animal

definitions.meaning: free of litter means tidy or orderly
an old word for an ox or cow, as in neatsfoot oil

explanation.surface: An animal that never has a litter of young.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a creature that bears no litters; really 'No litter' means tidy, and the second sense is the archaic word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidy describes a place without rubbish, and the archaic noun names bovine cattle.

clue.text: Councillor to go out for a chopping tool!

indicators.note: out here means placed on the outside, so the councillor's letters surround the departing verb

parts.note: Cr is an abbreviation for Councillor before a name
to leave is to go away

explanation.surface: A councillor storms off in search of a hatchet.
explanation.definitionFit: A butcher's heavy broad-bladed knife used for hacking through bone.

clue.text: Restlessness ruined a nice time round piano

indicators.note: round tells us the rearranged letters go around the next piece
ruined suggests something wrecked and broken up, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: the fodder taken as written
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A pleasant occasion around the piano was spoiled by fidgeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges A NICE TIME into IMATIENCE, and 'round' places it about P.
explanation.definitionFit: Impatience is a restless inability to wait calmly.

clue.text: We sat there embarrassing girlfriend

indicators.note: embarrassing is read as throwing into disorder, so the phrase is rearranged

parts.note: the fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: We sat there feeling awkward while someone's girlfriend looked on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embarrassing' turns WE SAT THERE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetheart is a beloved partner, a girlfriend or boyfriend.

clue.text: Bird from the Middle East in the south-west

indicators.note: in tells us one region's letters sit within the other's

parts.note: SW is the compass abbreviation for south-west
ME is the abbreviation for the Middle East

explanation.surface: A bird migrates from the Middle East to settle in the south-west.
explanation.walkthrough: The SMEW is a small duck of the merganser family.
explanation.definitionFit: The smew is a small diving duck, a winter visitor to Britain.

clue.text: Speak quite plainly and name the card correctly

definitions.meaning: to talk bluntly and frankly without euphemism
a literal reading: identify a playing card of the black suit by its true name

explanation.surface: A card player is told to be blunt and identify the card properly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being blunt; literally, it is announcing a card from that suit by its right name.

clue.text: See 10
Vehicle left-here perhaps

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
port is the nautical word for left

explanation.surface: A sign by a shelter saying a vehicle was left here.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'here perhaps': the place where a vehicle may be left, read from the whole clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A carport is a roofed open shelter where motorists park, the spot a parked motor sits.

clue.text: Where one shows a profit by all accounts

definitions.text: Where one shows a profit by all accounts

parts.words: Where one shows a profit by all accounts
parts.note: the phrase 'by all accounts' is literal: in bookkeeping ledgers, the column recording income and money owed to you

explanation.definitionFit: In double-entry accounting the right-hand column records receipts, so surplus appears there.

clue.text: Indignation of about ten fellows during the interval

indicators.note: during places the following pieces within the break

parts.note: a rest is a break or interval

indicators.note: about suggests moving things around, so these three letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder taken as written
men are fellows

explanation.surface: Ten men grumble with indignation through the half-time break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges TEN to ENT; with MEN it goes 'during' REST, splitting it as RES...T.
explanation.definitionFit: Resentment is bitter indignation at unfair treatment.

clue.text: Took, without approval, that French hat

indicators.note: without signals the approval word is removed from the verb before it

parts.note: taken as written
OK is an expression of approval
que is French for that

explanation.surface: Someone took a French hat without permission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes OK from TOOK, leaving TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A toque is a small brimless hat, as worn by chefs.

clue.text: Child ie removed during the Gaelic dance evening

indicators.note: removed is read as moved about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A youngster is taken away in the middle of a Scottish dance night.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceilidh is a Scottish or Irish social gathering with folk music and dancing.

clue.text: Stop in the place as expected

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A command to halt in the expected spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across plaCE AS Expected.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease is to come to a halt or end.

clue.text: One who is habitually full of spirit

definitions.text: One who is habitually full of spirit

parts.words: One who is habitually full of spirit
parts.note: looks like a lively person, but spirit means strong liquor: a regular heavy drinker

explanation.definitionFit: A toper is a chronic drunkard, someone routinely filled with alcohol.

clue.text: Girl coming from the jumble sale…

indicators.note: jumble means a muddle, so the next word's letters are mixed up

parts.note: the fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl arrives from the charity jumble sale.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumble sale is a British charity sale of second-hand goods; 'jumble' is the indicator here.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsa is a girl's name.

clue.text: … girl spotted behind the band

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as '… girl spotted behind the band (4)': no parse of 'behind the band' gives ANNA; likely an OCR misreading of a word.

clue.text: Broke open right inside the statue

indicators.note: inside places the abbreviation within the sculpture

parts.note: a bust is a sculpture of the head and shoulders

explanation.surface: Someone smashed open a statue to see what was in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To burst is to break apart suddenly from pressure.

clue.text: Spotted having a certain amount of discolouration

definitions.text: Spotted having a certain amount of discolouration

parts.words: Spotted having a certain amount of discolouration
parts.note: describes skin marked with patches of uneven colour

explanation.definitionFit: Something blotchy is covered in irregular stains or patches.

clue.text: Swingers' bar

parts.note: looks like a nightspot for partygoers, but means the horizontal bar acrobats swing on

explanation.definitionFit: A circus apparatus: a crossbar hung from two ropes for aerial acrobats.

clue.text: Humble soldier backing peer

indicators.note: backing tells us the soldier's two letters are read backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
a peer is a noble, a member of the nobility

explanation.surface: A lowly soldier gives support to an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignoble means of low birth or humble origin, as well as base.

clue.text: Tree Don uprooted was wearing away

indicators.note: uprooted suggests something torn up and disturbed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A tree that Don dug out was gradually decaying.
explanation.definitionFit: Erodent is an adjective meaning eroding, gradually destroying by abrasion.

clue.text: Guard fed up before the finish

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the fodder taken as written
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: A guard sick of things until the very end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FED into DEF; 'fed up' looks like boredom.
explanation.definitionFit: To defend is to guard or protect.

clue.text: Top meeting

parts.note: a gathering of heads of government, the highest-level talks; also read as peak plus discussion

explanation.definitionFit: Such a gathering brings together national leaders, the highest level of diplomacy.

clue.text: They are found in pants proverbially!

definitions.text: They are found in pants proverbially!

indicators.note: found in tells us the letters are contained in the next word

explanation.surface: A jokey reference to the saying about restless people having them in their trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ants in your pants' is a saying for restless fidgeting; the insects also sit inside the word pANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying about fidgety people names these insects as the cause.

clue.text: To practice crystal-gazing initially Sally creates runes yearly

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the opening letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: Sally carves runes once a year to read the future.
explanation.definitionFit: To scry is to foretell the future by gazing into a crystal ball.

clue.text: See 24
Finished at 500 to!

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Finished at 500 to! (4)': D for 500 is clear, but 'at ... to' gives no ONE; likely an OCR misreading.

clue.text: The recent past, it belongs to 24 hours ago

definitions.meaning: the plural noun means times just gone by
a possessive reading: of the day before today

explanation.surface: A remark on recent times and what belongs to the previous day.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the day before today means bygone times; with an apostrophe it is that day's possessive.
